objects.description: Abstract interface for pluggable logging backends in the Util namespace. Implementations provide the log(tag, fmt, va_list) method which is called by the logging helpers; returns true if the message was handled. Lifetime is managed by the user; a pointer can be set per-thread via set_thread_logging_interface.

Small utility struct in the Internal namespace that determines at construction time whether the current Linux process is being traced by a debugger by parsing /proc/self/status (TracerPid). The state field is true if a debugger is attached.

functions.name: Util::LoggingInterface::~LoggingInterface
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Util::LoggingInterface. Ensures proper cleanup via base-class pointers when deleting objects implementing the logging interface. Typically invoked implicitly when a LoggingInterface-derived instance goes out of scope or is deleted.
requirements: The object must be a valid, fully constructed instance of a class derived from Util::LoggingInterface at the time of destruction

functions.name: Util::LoggingInterface::log
functions.signature: virtual bool Util::LoggingInterface::log(const char *tag, const char *fmt, va_list va) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual method that concrete logging backends must implement. Logs a message given a tag, a printf-style format string, and a va_list of arguments. Return value indicates whether the message was handled.
requirements: tag must be a valid, null-terminated C string
fmt must be a valid, null-terminated printf-style format string
va must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to fmt
Implementations should return true if the message was successfully handled, false otherwise

functions.name: Util::interface_log
functions.description: Thread-aware logging entry point that attempts to log using the current thread’s LoggingInterface. Accepts a tag and a printf-style format string with variadic arguments. Returns true if a logging interface handled the message; otherwise false so callers can fall back to another logging mechanism.
requirements: tag must be a valid, null-terminated C string
fmt must be a valid, null-terminated printf-style format string
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt
Callers should check the boolean return value to decide whether to perform a fallback log path

functions.name: Util::set_thread_logging_interface
functions.description: Sets the thread-local logging interface used by interface_log for the current thread. Typically used to install or change the logging backend for a thread.
requirements: iface must point to a valid Util::LoggingInterface instance whose lifetime exceeds any subsequent calls to interface_log on this thread; passing nullptr behavior is unknown from this header

functions.name: Internal::is_debugged
functions.description: Checks whether the current process is being debugged. On non-MSVC builds, it inspects /proc/self/status and reads TracerPid to detect an attached debugger. Used to decide whether to trigger a debug trap.
requirements: Available and functional only on non-MSVC platforms (guarded by #ifndef _MSC_VER)
Requires readable /proc/self/status on platforms that provide it

functions.name: debug_break
functions.description: Triggers a debugger break/trap if a debugger is attached, using platform-appropriate mechanisms. On MSVC, uses IsDebuggerPresent and __debugbreak; on some GCC/Clang Unix targets, uses an int3 or builtin trap when a debugger is detected.
requirements: Intended for debug contexts; behavior depends on platform and presence of a debugger
On non-MSVC GCC Linux x86, only triggers if Internal::is_debugged() returns true

endpoints.name: Util::LoggingInterface::~LoggingInterface
Util::interface_log
Util::set_thread_logging_interface
Internal::is_debugged

unharnessable_functions.name: Util::LoggingInterface::log
unharnessable_functions.reason: The method is pure virtual and requires a valid va_list, which cannot be safely constructed without defining a variadic helper function.

unharnessable_functions.name: debug_break
unharnessable_functions.reason: Invoking it can trigger a trap/SIGTRAP and terminate the fuzzer process if a debugger is detected, making it unsafe to harness.

data_types.description: A null-terminated sequence of bytes interpreted as a C-style string. May contain arbitrary bytes except that a terminating NUL (\0) marks the end. Used for parameters expecting const char* such as tags or general text.

A null-terminated C string interpreted by printf-style formatting functions. Contains ordinary characters and optional % conversion specifiers that must match the provided variadic arguments (e.g., %d, %s, %x, %zu). Should not contain invalid or mismatched specifiers.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate bytes that will be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and generic integer parameters.
# The fuzzer stub uses:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for tag
# - mode = *FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) % 4
# - possibly another FUZZ_PARAM_STR() when mode==2
# - FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for values
# Our buffer should therefore encode a sequence the harness can split into these items.
# Common fuzz harnesses map FUZZ_PARAM_STR to pulling a length-prefixed or NUL-terminated
# slice from the input. To maximize compatibility while keeping inputs valid C strings,
# we emit a simple concatenation of NUL-terminated strings and fixed-width integers.
#
# Layout we produce (in order):
# 1) tag_str: NUL-terminated C string (printable with some edge cases)
# 2) mode: 4 bytes little-endian unsigned int
# 3) Depending on mode:
#    - mode 0: no extra
#    - mode 1: int v (4 bytes LE)
#    - mode 2: second string s: NUL-terminated C string
#    - mode 3: two unsigned ints x (4 bytes LE) and n (4 bytes LE)
#
# Notes:
# - We keep strings reasonably small and vary content to explore odd/even tag lengths (affects return path).
# - We ensure all strings are valid C strings by terminating with NUL and avoiding embedded NULs.
# - Integers are generated across a wide range.
# - Total size limited to <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-./:@[]{}(),+*=<>!?%# "


def _rand(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_c_string(rng: random.Random, target_len: int, ensure_even_length: bool | None = None) -> bytes:
    # Generate a C string of length target_len (not including NUL) with printable chars.
    # Optionally enforce even/odd length to hit different FuzzLogger return paths.
    if target_len < 0:
        target_len = 0
    length = target_len
    if ensure_even_length is not None:
        if ensure_even_length and (length % 2) != 0:
            length += 1
        if not ensure_even_length and (length % 2) == 0:
            length = max(1, length + 1)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"


def _u32_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return int(x & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False)


def _i32_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return int(x & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False)


def _choose_modes(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias to cover all modes frequently
    weights = [1, 1, 1, 1]
    # Occasionally emphasize mode 2 and 3 which have extra params
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        weights = [1, 1, 2, 2]
    total = sum(weights)
    pick = rng.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for i, w in enumerate(weights):
        acc += w
        if pick < acc:
            return i
    return rng.randrange(4)


def _tag_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Provide some interesting tags: empty, short, long, with spaces and punctuation
    tags = [
        b"\x00",  # empty tag
        b"a\x00",
        b"even\x00",  # even length (4)
        b"odd\x00",   # odd length (3)
        b"INFO\x00",
        b"WARN:net\x00",
        b"render-thread\x00",
        b"io.worker.7\x00",
        ("X" * 63).encode() + b"\x00",  # long but < 256
        ("Y" * 128).encode() + b"\x00",
    ]
    # Random tag with controlled parity to toggle return value
    want_even = rng.choice([True, False])
    rand_len = rng.randint(0, 40)
    tags.append(_make_c_string(rng, rand_len, ensure_even_length=want_even))
    return tags


def _second_string_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    s = [
        b"hello\x00",
        b"\x00",  # empty string
        b"% not a spec, literal percent\x00",
        b"Some UTF-8: \xE2\x9C\x93\x00",
        ("A" * rng.randint(1, 200)).encode() + b"\x00",
    ]
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()

    # 1) Tag string
    tag = rng.choice(_tag_candidates(rng))
    out += tag

    # 2) Mode
    mode = _choose_modes(rng)
    out += _u32_le(mode)

    # 3) Mode-specific payload
    if mode == 1:
        # int v for "%d"
        # Cover both small and large, positive/negative values
        choices = [0, 1, -1, 42, -42, 2**31 - 1, -2**31]
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            v = rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)
        else:
            v = rng.choice(choices)
        out += _i32_le(v)
    elif mode == 2:
        # string s for "%s"
        s = rng.choice(_second_string_candidates(rng))
        out += s
    elif mode == 3:
        # unsigned int x for %x and size_t n for %zu (we'll provide 32-bit; harness likely reads u32)
        # x spans full range; n limited to 0..1023 in stub, but we provide general values;
        # the stub masks n to 0..1023 anyway.
        x_choices = [0, 1, 0x7fffffff, 0xffffffff, rng.getrandbits(32)]
        x = rng.choice(x_choices)
        n_choices = [0, 1, 15, 255, 1023, 4095, rng.getrandbits(32)]
        n = rng.choice(n_choices)
        out += _u32_le(x)
        out += _u32_le(n)

    # Limit size
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid C strings intended for use as:
# - tag strings (arbitrary text, null-terminated when consumed by the fuzzer framework)
# - printf format strings with arguments chosen by the stub itself
#
# The target fuzzer stub constructs its own format strings and provides matching
# arguments. Our job is to provide interesting yet valid data for FUZZ_PARAM_STR,
# primarily the tag and the optional string argument when mode==2.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a buffer that concatenates multiple null-terminated strings so the
#   FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumer can slice different segments. We keep total size <= 4096.
# - Include a broad variety of tags: empty, very short, very long, even/odd length
#   (affects FuzzLogger return), ASCII, Unicode-like UTF-8, whitespace, punctuation,
#   and paths. Also include strings containing percent signs that are safe ("%%") so
#   they won't be treated as format specifiers if re-used as fmt.
# - Include some strings with embedded NUL terminators by delimiting items with \0.
#   The fuzzer framework typically treats FUZZ_PARAM_STR as a C string from the
#   current cursor, so multiple items give it multiple choices as input evolves.
# - Avoid invalid UTF-8 and avoid unmatched printf specifiers in case a string is
#   ever used as a format string; we escape single % as %%.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:@#,+="

COMMON_TAGS = [
    "",  # empty
    "a",  # odd length
    "ab",  # even length
    "main",
    "io",
    "render",
    "network",
    "dbg",
    "info",
    "warn",
    "error",
    "trace",
    "util",
    "thread",
    "logger",
]

UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "αβγ",        # Greek
    "日本語",       # Japanese
    "emoji_😀",    # Emoji
    "русский",     # Cyrillic
    "arabic_مرحبا",
]

PATHS = [
    "/", "/tmp", "/var/log/app", "C:/Windows/System32", "..", "./relative/path",
]

SAFE_PERCENT_SAMPLES = [
    "percent_100%%",  # literal percent
    "mix%%-tag",
    "end%%",
]

WHITESPACEY = [
    " ", "\t\t", "\n", " tag\nwith\nnewlines ", " leading ", "trailing ", " middle spaced ",
]

LONG_BLOCKS = [
    "A" * 1,
    "B" * 2,
    "C" * 15,
    "D" * 64,
    "E" * 127,
    "F" * 255,
    "G" * 512,
]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _escape_single_percents(s: str) -> str:
    # Replace single % with %% to keep strings safe if interpreted as format strings.
    # Do not touch existing %% sequences.
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == '%':
            if i + 1 < len(s) and s[i + 1] == '%':
                out.append('%%')
                i += 2
            else:
                out.append('%%')
                i += 1
        else:
            out.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return ''.join(out)


def _build_items(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    items: List[bytes] = []

    # Core common tags
    for t in COMMON_TAGS:
        items.append(t.encode('utf-8'))

    # Whitespace-focused
    for t in WHITESPACEY:
        items.append(t.encode('utf-8'))

    # Paths
    for p in PATHS:
        items.append(p.encode('utf-8'))

    # Unicode snippets and combinations
    for u in UNICODE_SNIPPETS:
        items.append(u.encode('utf-8'))
    # Mixed unicode + ascii
    for u in UNICODE_SNIPPETS:
        items.append((u + "-" + _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8)).encode('utf-8'))

    # Safe percent samples
    for s in SAFE_PERCENT_SAMPLES:
        items.append(s.encode('utf-8'))

    # Random ascii samples with safe percent escaping
    for _ in range(12):
        raw = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 48)
        raw = raw[: rng.randint(0, len(raw))]
        raw = raw + ("%" if rng.random() < 0.3 else "")
        items.append(_escape_single_percents(raw).encode('utf-8'))

    # Long blocks to hit buffer boundaries and even/odd lengths
    for lb in LONG_BLOCKS:
        items.append(lb.encode('utf-8'))

    # Crafted even/odd length toggles
    for base in ["t", "tag", "even", "odd"]:
        for k in range(4):
            s = base + ("_" * k)
            items.append(s.encode('utf-8'))

    # A few strings containing format-like text but escaped
    fmt_like = [
        "value_%d_here",
        "hex_%x_num",
        "size_%zu_units",
        "multi_%d_%x_%zu",
    ]
    for f in fmt_like:
        items.append(_escape_single_percents(f).encode('utf-8'))

    # Very long mixed string under limit
    big = (
        "TAG_" + _rand_ascii(rng, 32, 256) + "_" + rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS) + "_" + rng.choice(SAFE_PERCENT_SAMPLES)
    )
    items.append(big.encode('utf-8'))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[bytes] = []
    for it in items:
        if it not in seen:
            uniq.append(it)
            seen.add(it)
    return uniq


def _join_cstrings(items: List[bytes], max_total: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated C strings: item + '\0' + ... + final '\0'
    out = bytearray()
    # Randomize order slightly
    items = items[:]  # copy
    rng.shuffle(items)

    # Always ensure we include a couple of guaranteed varieties first
    must = [b"", b"ab", b"abc", b"percent_100%%"]
    for m in must:
        if m not in items:
            items.insert(0, m)
    # Build
    for it in items:
        need = len(it) + 1  # plus NUL
        if len(out) + need > max_total:
            break
        out += it
        out.append(0)
    # Ensure final NUL terminator (already ensured by loop)
    if not out or out[-1] != 0:
        out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    items = _build_items(rng)
    buf = _join_cstrings(items, MAX_TOTAL, rng)
    return buf
